title: Homepage value hooks: latency, cost, and operational guarantees — copy & test plan
content:
Purpose
Draft a set of homepage/hero and product-section copy variants that prioritize different value hooks (latency control, predictable unit economics, and operational reliability). This is a working brief for short-run experiments (2-week test windows) and for input into the design sprint on 2026-03-15.

Audience and hypothesis
Primary audience: engineering-led buyers (CTOs, platform engineers, ML infra). Secondary: product teams evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private inference.
Hypothesis: Lead with an engineer-first economic claim + a concrete latency guarantee will increase click-through to pricing/benchmarks by ~15% vs a generic "fast and reliable" hero.

What success looks like (metrics)
- CTA click-through to "Performance benchmarks" or "See pricing": +15% lift target
- Avg time on product page: +10% (engagement with performance table)
- Signups from self-serve: +10% (qualified by "uses LLM in product" in onboarding)

Hero variants (short lines for designer handoff)
1) Precision-first (latency SLA focus)
- Headline: "Predictable latency for real products"
- Subhead: "Ship features that behave. SLO-backed inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- CTA primary: "See latency guarantees"; CTA secondary: "Run our benchmark"
- Notes: emphasize SLO, can call out "p99 under Xms on common models" in adjacent subpanel (placeholder).

2) Unit-economics (cost transparency)
- Headline: "Inference that scales costs, not surprises"
- Subhead: "Engineering controls to lower token costs: batching, caching, and quantization profiles tuned per workload."
- CTA primary: "Estimate my cost"; CTA secondary: "Optimization guide"
- Notes: callouts to dedicated pricing and Optimize features. Include an abbreviated cost-savings stat (e.g., "typical customers save 2–5x vs raw GPU") — mark as claim-to-validate.

3) Reliability-first (fallbacks and graceful degradation)
- Headline: "Keep features online, even when models or regions fail"
- Subhead: "Automated fallbacks, model routing, and canary rollouts to prevent outages during inference spikes."
- CTA primary: "How fallbacks work"; CTA secondary: "Request an SLA"

4) Developer velocity (single API across environments)
- Headline: "One API. Any deployment."
- Subhead: "Same SDK and operational tooling for hosted, dedicated, and private—so teams move faster without re-architecting."
- CTA primary: "See the SDK"; CTA secondary: "Migration checklist"

Hero test matrix (two-week window per variant)
- Variant groups: Precision-first vs Unit-economics vs Reliability-first vs Developer-velocity (control: existing hero copy).
- Traffic split: 25% each of organic homepage visitors for 2 weeks (target N>1200 per variant).
- Primary metric: CTA click-through to corresponding deep-dive. Secondary metric: signup flow conversion.

Product page sections (modular copy blocks)
1) Performance and SLAs
- Lead paragraph: "Performance you can depend on—SLOs, high-throughput kernels, and KV caching that reduces latency while keeping costs down."
- Bullets: "p99 latency SLOs; hardware-aware kernel selection; continuous batching that respects SLOs and tail latency"
- Visual cue: small benchmark table + link to complete perf data.

2) Cost controls and Optimize
- Lead paragraph: "Control cost at the unit level—intelligent batching, caching, and model profiles give you levers to trade latency for dollars."
- Bullets: "Policy-driven routing (cost vs latency); quantization recommendations by workload; per-route cost dashboards"

3) Deployment modes (Hosted | Dedicated | Private)
- Short declarative lead: "Same API across three deployment modes."
- Subsections: one-liners and a single-row benefits table for each mode (security, SLA, volume).

4) Reliability and rollouts
- Lead paragraph: "Safe rollouts and automatic fallbacks—reduce blast radius and avoid outages during traffic spikes."
- Bullets: "Canary & A/B rollouts, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, cross-region failover"

5) Eval-driven quality assurance
- Copy: "Tie regressions to tests and prompts: preflight evaluation suites prevent quality surprises at rollout."

Competitive angle notes (quick sensemaking)
- Cloud AI endpoints (large providers): easy onboarding but opaque costs and limited production controls. Positioning: "More production controls and transparent economics than public clouds."
- LLM API incumbents (simplicity-focused vendors): friendly dev UX but inconsistent SLOs for high-throughput apps. Positioning: "Same developer ergonomics, plus SLOs and optimization levers for production."
- Self-hosted inference runtimes (open-source): flexible and low-level control but heavy ops burden. Positioning: "Provide managed tooling, standardized observability, and optional private deployments without building infra from scratch."

Key objection handling (for FAQ/snippets)
- "Why not just run models on VMs?" -> "You can, but our runtime optimizes batching, KV cache reuse, and kernel selection automatically, saving ops time and per-token dollars."
- "How do you measure cost savings?" -> "We report per-route token cost, recommend quantization profiles, and run evals to ensure quality is retained—customers typically see 2–5x improvements depending on workload architecture."
- "What if I need on-prem?" -> "Private deployment is supported with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped packaging."

Open questions and research tasks (action items)
- Validate the "2–5x cost savings" stat: ask Applied ML for cohort report by 2026-03-20 (Owner: Mateo).
- Create a small p99 latency claim set by model family and size for the hero microcopy (Owner: SRE team request; PR: SRE-146).
- Design needs: short visual for fallbacks/rollouts and a micro-animation for "one API across environments" (Owner: Product design).
- Legal: review phrasing around SLAs and "guarantees" before copy goes live (Owner: Legal — deadline 2026-03-18).

Microcopy experiments (quick variants to A/B)
- CTA language alternatives: "See latency guarantees" vs "View benchmarks" vs "Run your model" (test conversion depth).
- Value paragraph length: 18–32 words vs 40–60 words (test engagement/time-on-page).

Notes to design/content sync
- Keep hero headline under 7 words when possible for mobile.
- Use numeric claims sparingly and always link to supporting benchmark page. Mark claims behind a tooltip for legal/accuracy.
- Prioritize developer-facing language (SDK, API, SLO) on initial fold; secondary fold can borrow business/exec phrasing for enterprise buyers.

Draft micro-FAQ (for product panel)
Q: "Will my latency vary by region?"
A: "Yes — we surface region-level perf and route requests by policy; cross-region failover keeps features available."
Q: "How do you protect model privacy in Private deployments?"
A: "Customer-managed VPCs plus KMS/HSM integrations; we do not surface data to shared tenants."

Appendix: links for reference
- Benchmark repository (internal): CONFLUENCE-6791-homepage-metrics
- Optimize feature spec (early draft): GIT-PR-2308
- Slack thread: #product-homepage (thread id abc123)

Bottom line / next steps
1) Sync with Applied ML and SRE to validate numeric claims and produce a compact benchmark panel (due 2026-03-20).
2) Hand hero variants to design for visual exploration by 2026-03-12 (priority: Precision-first and Unit-economics).
3) Set up experiment in LaunchDarkly/AB tool and measurement dashboard (GTM) for a 2-week run starting 2026-03-22.

Working notes (scratch)
- Consider a micro-interaction that shows "predicted per-token cost" for a sample prompt — may increase click-to-pricing.
- Taglines that sound too marketing-y ("inference for the modern era") should be avoided in favor of concrete engineering benefits.
- Iterate headlines in plain language—engineers respond better to numeric and operational signals.
